utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see that the parties are as before. This is the oral ruling of the Trial Chamber on the Rule 98 bis motion by the Defence. The Trial Chamber is seized of motions for acquittal filed pursuant to 98 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence by the three accused, Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric. The Office of the Prosecutor filed its confidential response on 27th September, this year. The public redacted response of the Prosecution was accepted by the Trial Chamber as validly filed pursuant to Rule 127(A)(ii) of the rules by decision of 2nd October. All three accused in this case have moved for total acquittal pursuant to 98 bis with respect to all the charges brought against them in the Fifth Amended Indictment. The accused have also requested that they be heard orally on the motions. However, the Trial Chamber is of the view that the written motions and the response of the Prosecutor have sufficiently put forward the arguments of the parties and therefore further oral argument will not be necessary. Having reviewed the arguments of the parties, the Trial Chamber will now render its decision. The written decision of the Trial Chamber will be issued in due course. The standard which this Trial Chamber has applied is that laid down by the Appeals Chamber in the case of the Prosecutor versus Jelesic which is whether there is evidence, if accepted, upon which a reasonable Tribunal of fact could be satisfied beyond reasonable doubt of the guilt of the accused on the particular charge in question. On the basis of this standard, the Trial Chamber has directed its attention to the submissions of the parties concerning the specific allegations in the Fifth Amended Indictment. In brief, the indictment charges the three accused with persecution as a crime against humanity, that is Count 1, pursuant to Article 5(h) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 7(1). The underlying acts to support this charge include the forcible takeover of the municipality of Bosanski Samac, the unlawful arrest, detention, and confinement of non-Serb civilians; the cruel and inhumane treatment, including beatings, torture, and forced labour of non-Serb civilians; the deportation, forcible transfer, and expulsion of non-Serb civilians; the wanton and extensive destruction, plundering, and looting of property, and the destruction or wilful damage of institutions dedicated to religion. Blagoje Simic is further charged with the issuance of orders or policies which violated the rights of non-Serbs, while Simo Zaric is further charged with the interrogation of non-Serb civilians who had been arrested or detained and with forcing them to sign forced and coerced statements. Both the accused have challenged the sufficiency of evidence with regard to the factual allegations contained in Count 1. In addition, they have raised challenges concerning the discriminatory intent required under Count 1 and challenged the allegation that they had acted in concert together with others to commit the crimes alleged in Count 1. Having reviewed the evidence and the submissions of the parties, the Trial Chamber finds that sufficient evidence exists, if accepted, upon which a reasonable Tribunal of fact could be satisfied beyond reasonable doubt of the guilt of Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric with respect to the forcible takeover as contained in paragraphs 13(a), 14(a) and 15(a) of the indictment; the unlawful arrests and confinement as contained in paragraphs 13(c), 14(b) and 15(b) of the indictment; the cruel and inhumane treatment as contained in paragraphs 13(d), 14(c) and 15(c); the deportation, forcible transfer, and expulsion as contained in paragraphs 13(e), 14(d) and 15(e). The Trial Chamber finds that there is sufficient evidence on the further charges against Blagoje Simic under paragraphs 13(b) and Simo Zaric under paragraphs 15(d) of the indictment. In relation to the offence of wanton and extensive destruction, plundering, and looting contained in paragraph 13(f), 14(e) and 15(f) of the indictment, the Trial Chamber finds that the Prosecution has presented evidence that provides a sufficient basis, if accepted, upon which a reasonable Tribunal of fact could be satisfied beyond a reasonable doubt of the involvement of Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric in the wanton and extensive plundering and looting of the property of Bosnian Croats, Bosnian Muslims, and the other non-Serb civilians, including dwellings, businesses, personal property and livestock. However, in the case of destruction, the evidence does not specifically link any of the accused persons to the destruction of dwellings, businesses, personal property, or livestock. Several Prosecution witnesses testified to such destruction having taken place but no further evidence was adduced linking the accused persons to the offence. The Trial Chamber thus finds that there is insufficient evidence concerning the involvement of all three accused in the wanton and extensive destruction of the property of Bosnian Croats, Bosnian Muslims, and the other non-Serb civilians, including dwellings, businesses, personal property, and livestock. There is, therefore, no case for them to answer in relation to the aspect of destruction in paragraphs 13(f), 14(e), and 15(f) of the indictment. In relation to the offence of destruction and wilful damage of institutions dedicated to religion contained in paragraphs 13(g), 14(f) and 15(g) of the indictment, the Trial Chamber is not satisfied that the totality of the evidence provides a sufficient basis upon which the Trial Chamber can put the accused on their defence in relation to this particular offence. The Trial Chamber finds that although there is evidence on the destruction of religious institutions, there is insufficient evidence on the link between the accused and the alleged destruction of the religious institutions. Accordingly, the accused have no case to answer concerning the whole offence of destruction and wilful damage to institutions dedicated to religion as contained in paragraphs 13(g), 14(f), and 15(g) of the indictment. On the issue of the requisite discriminatory intent for Count 1 based on the Trial Chamber's findings as just stated for this count, there is therefore sufficient evidence, if accepted, upon which a reasonable Tribunal could be satisfied beyond reasonable doubt that Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric possessed the necessary discriminatory intent to sustain a conviction for the crime of persecution as a crime against humanity. Counts 2 and 3: The indictment charges all three accused with deportation as a crime against humanity pursuant to Article 5(d) of the Statute under Count 2 and unlawful deportation or transfer, as a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, pursuant to Article 2(g) of the Statute under Count 3. Having reviewed the evidence and the submission of the parties, the Trial Chamber finds that there is sufficient evidence to put all three accused on their defence for the crimes of deportation as a crime against humanity and unlawful deportation or transfer as a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions under Counts 2 and 3 respectively. The above finding of "no case to answer" in those parts of paragraphs 13(f), 14(e) and 15(f) and the whole of paragraphs 13(g), 14(f), 15(g), do not affect the integrity of persecution as a crime against humanity under Count 1 of the indictment, as the rest of the factual allegations still stand. For the foregoing reasons and pursuant to 98 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, the Trial Chamber enters a judgement of acquittal and -- enters a judgement of acquittal in respect of the aspect of destruction of the property of Bosnian Croats, Bosnian Muslims, and the other non-Serb civilians, including dwellings, businesses, personal property, and livestock, as contained in paragraphs 13(f), 14(e), and 15(f) of the indictment, and on the whole offence of destruction or wilful damage of institutions dedicated to religion as contained in paragraphs 13(g), 14(f) and 15(g) of the indictment. The rest of the motions for acquittal are dismissed. There being no other business, the Court will rise.
